message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.1","text":"So, when two days had passed and the third was beginning to dawn, I, Clement, awoke for the debate with Simon, and together with the companions who were with me, at the second calls of the roosters, we found the lamp still shining and Peter on his knees praying. When he had finished his petition, he turned, saw that we were ready to listen, and said:","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὸ διαλεχθῆναι τῷ Σίμωνι","chosen":"for the debate with Simon","rationale":"διαλέγεσθαι can denote discussion or debate; the planned public dispute supports “debate.”"},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τὰς δευτέρας τῶν ἀλεκτρυόνων φωνάς","chosen":"at the second calls of the roosters","rationale":"This preserves the reference to the second round of rooster calls rather than replacing it with a conventional time designation."},{"source_quote":"τὸν δὲ Πέτρον γονυκλινῆ προσευχόμενον","chosen":"Peter on his knees praying","rationale":"γονυκλινής describes a kneeling posture."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.2","text":"“I want you to know that those who, under our direction, associate with Simon so that, as they learn his plans, they may report them to us, enabling us to adapt ourselves to the variety of his wickedness, have themselves sent word and informed us, saying: ‘Today Simon, just as he arranged, is ready to come before everyone and demonstrate from the Scriptures that this one is not the highest God—he “who created heaven and earth” and all things in them—but that there is some other unknown and highest one, as one existing among secret mysteries, a God of gods. He sent two gods, of whom one is the one who created the world, while the other is the one who gave the law. Simon schemes to say these things so that he may undermine beforehand the right faith of those who are going to worship the one and only God, “who created heaven and earth.”’”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"καθ’ ἡμετέραν πρόνοιαν","chosen":"under our direction","rationale":"In context πρόνοια refers to the deliberate arrangement by which the informants remain with Simon; “by our foresight” is also lexically possible."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὴν τῆς κακίας αὐτοῦ ποικιλίαν ἁρμόσασθαι","chosen":"adapt ourselves to the variety of his wickedness","rationale":"ποικιλία denotes variety or versatility, while ἁρμόζεσθαι expresses adjustment to it."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἐν ἀπορρήτοις ὄντα θεὸν θεῶν","chosen":"as one existing among secret mysteries, a God of gods","rationale":"ἀπόρρητα can denote secrets, mysteries, or esoteric teachings. Here ὡς introduces the characterization attributed to Simon; alternatives include “supposedly existing among secret things as God of gods.”"},{"source_quote":"προεκλύσει","chosen":"may undermine beforehand","rationale":"The compound verb indicates loosening or weakening in advance."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μὴ τοῦτον εἶναι·θεὸν ἀνώτατον","issue":"The printed high point interrupts the infinitive construction between εἶναι and its predicate θεὸν ἀνώτατον. The surviving words yield a clear construction when repunctuated.","proposed_reading":"μὴ τοῦτον εἶναι θεὸν ἀνώτατον","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τῶν τὸν ἕνα καὶ μόνον μελλόντων. σέβειν θεόν","issue":"The printed full stop separates μέλλειν from its complementary infinitive σέβειν. The translation treats this as intrusive editorial punctuation.","proposed_reading":"τῶν τὸν ἕνα καὶ μόνον μελλόντων σέβειν θεόν","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.3","text":"“When I heard these things, how could I not have been disheartened? Therefore I also wanted you, the brothers who are with me, to know that my soul is in no small pain, as I observe that the evil one is vigilant for the testing of human beings, while human beings are utterly neglectful of their own salvation. For he has contrived to introduce notions of many other gods among those from the nations who are about to be persuaded that the earthly carved images are not gods, so that, if they cease from the polytheistic madness below, they will be deceived into speaking in another way—or even worse—against God’s sole sovereignty, so that, never having preferred what belongs to that sole sovereignty, they may never at any time be able to obtain mercy. For this audacious undertaking Simon approaches us for battle, armed with the false passages of the Scriptures. And what is worse, on the basis of prophets in whom he has not believed, he has not feared to teach such doctrines against the God who truly is.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς ἑαυτῶν σωτηρίας πάνυ ἀμελοῦντας","chosen":"utterly neglectful of their own salvation","rationale":"πάνυ intensifies the stated neglect and is retained rather than softened."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἐπιγείων ξοάνων","chosen":"the earthly carved images","rationale":"ξόανα are carved cult images; “earthly” preserves the contrast expressed by ἐπίγειος."},{"source_quote":"τῆς κάτω πολυθέου μανίας","chosen":"the polytheistic madness below","rationale":"The spatial image of κάτω is retained; alternatives include “earthbound polytheistic madness” and “polytheistic madness down here.”"},{"source_quote":"τῆς· τοῦ θεοῦ μοναρχίας","chosen":"God’s sole sovereignty","rationale":"μοναρχία here denotes the rule or sovereignty of the one God. The rendering disregards the intrusive printed high point but does not alter the surviving words."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα μηδέποτε τὰ τῆς μοναρχίας προτιμήσαντες οὐπώποτε ἐλέους τυχεῖν δυνηθῶσιν","chosen":"so that, never having preferred what belongs to that sole sovereignty, they may never at any time be able to obtain mercy","rationale":"Both negative expressions, μηδέποτε and οὐπώποτε, are preserved rather than reducing their apparent repetition."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ὄντως θεοῦ","chosen":"the God who truly is","rationale":"This reflects ὄντως as an assertion of actual existence; “the true God” is a smoother possible rendering but is less source-transparent."},{"source_quote":"ἀφ’ ὧν οὐ πεπίστευκε προφητῶν","chosen":"on the basis of prophets in whom he has not believed","rationale":"The relative is attracted into the case of its antecedent προφητῶν. “From prophets whom he has not believed” is also possible."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"κατὰ τῆς· τοῦ θεοῦ μοναρχίας","issue":"The printed high point separates the article τῆς from its dependent genitive τοῦ θεοῦ and is syntactically intrusive. The phrase remains intelligible when repunctuated.","proposed_reading":"κατὰ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ μοναρχίας","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.4","text":"“As for us, who have inherited from our ancestors both the worship of the God who created everything and, further, the mystery of the books capable of deceiving, he will be able to accomplish nothing. But among those from the nations, who have the polytheistic conception as a companion from their upbringing and do not know the false elements in the Scriptures, he will be capable of much—not only he; even if someone else presents to those from the nations, against God, some empty, ornamented myth resembling a sumptuous dream, that person too will be believed, because from childhood their mind has been accustomed to accept the things said against God. Yet there will indeed be some rare ones among them—few out of a multitude—who, through good sense, will not be willing even so much as merely to hear an evil word against the God who created everything. For these alone, though they are from the nations, it will come about that they are saved. Therefore, let none of you blame Simon at all, or anyone else either, for nothing happens unjustly, seeing that even the false elements in the Scriptures turn out reasonably to serve as a test.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῶν ἀπατᾶν δυναμένων βίβλων τὸ μυστήριον","chosen":"the mystery of the books capable of deceiving","rationale":"The rendering preserves both the books’ stated capacity to deceive and the unexplained “mystery” associated with them."},{"source_quote":"τὴν πολύθεον ὑπόληψιν· σύντροφον ἔχουσιν","chosen":"have the polytheistic conception as a companion from their upbringing","rationale":"σύντροφος can describe something reared together with a person and thus ingrained from upbringing, not merely a temporary companion. The printed high point is treated as intrusive."},{"source_quote":"ὅμοιον ὀνείρῳ πλουσίῳ, κεκοσμημένον","chosen":"ornamented ... resembling a sumptuous dream","rationale":"πλούσιος is rendered “sumptuous” to convey a richly furnished dream; “a rich dream” is the more literal alternative."},{"source_quote":"δι’ εὐγνωμοσύνην","chosen":"through good sense","rationale":"εὐγνωμοσύνη here denotes sound or fair-minded judgment; “upright-mindedness” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"κακὸν. λόγον αὐτὸ κἂν ἀκοῦσαι μόνον","chosen":"even so much as merely to hear an evil word","rationale":"The printed stop is treated as intrusive, and αὐτό is understood adverbially or intensively with “hear merely.” If it were construed as agreeing directly with λόγον, masculine αὐτόν would be expected."},{"source_quote":"παντελῶς μεμφέσθω","chosen":"blame ... at all","rationale":"With the negative imperative, παντελῶς can mean “at all”; “blame altogether” or “blame utterly” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"εὐλόγως πρὸς δοκιμὴν ἔχοντα τυγχάνει","chosen":"turn out reasonably to serve as a test","rationale":"The idiom presents the false elements as having a rationally explicable testing function."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὴν πολύθεον ὑπόληψιν· σύντροφον ἔχουσιν","issue":"The printed high point interrupts the construction in which σύντροφον is the complement of ἔχουσιν with τὴν πολύθεον ὑπόληψιν as its object. The translation repunctuates without changing the surviving words.","proposed_reading":"τὴν πολύθεον ὑπόληψιν σύντροφον ἔχουσιν","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"κακὸν. λόγον αὐτὸ κἂν ἀκοῦσαι μόνον","issue":"The printed full stop separates κακόν from λόγον and is syntactically intrusive. The neuter αὐτό is also unusual if taken as an adjective modifying masculine λόγον, but it can defensibly be read adverbially or intensively, so no lexical emendation is adopted.","proposed_reading":"κακὸν λόγον αὐτὸ κἂν ἀκοῦσαι μόνον","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.5","text":"And when I, Clement, heard this, I said, “What do you mean, lord, by saying that even the false elements in the Scriptures reasonably serve to test human beings?” He answered, “The false elements of the Scriptures were permitted to be written, at wickedness’s request, for a certain just reason. Here is what I mean by ‘reasonably’: In discussions about God, a wicked person, though loving God no less than a good person does, falls short of the good person in one respect only: he does not pardon even those who act impiously because of ignorance, but out of affection for what is being treated impiously, he desires the destruction of those who act impiously and does not even offer them healing. For the good person wants everyone to be healed through changes of heart, but saves only those who have come to know God. Those who do not know, however, he does not heal—not because he does not want to, but because it is not permissible to grant the good things prepared for the sons of the kingdom to those who, because of their lack of discernment, have been likened to irrational animals.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Τὰ ψευδῆ τῶν γραφῶν","chosen":"The false elements of the Scriptures","rationale":"The substantivized adjective refers to what is false within the Scriptures; “the falsehoods of the Scriptures” is possible but can imply that the Scriptures as a whole are characterized as false."},{"source_quote":"αἰτήματι κακίας","chosen":"at wickedness’s request","rationale":"The genitive presents wickedness as the source or possessor of the request; the personification is retained."},{"source_quote":"δικαίῳ τινὶ λόγῳ","chosen":"for a certain just reason","rationale":"λόγος here can denote reason, rationale, or account; the dative states the just rationale under which the writing was permitted."},{"source_quote":"ἐν ταῖς θεολογίαις","chosen":"In discussions about God","rationale":"The plural can refer to discourses or deliberations concerning God; “in theological matters” is a more technical alternative."},{"source_quote":"ὁ πονηρὸς τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ","chosen":"a wicked person ... a good person","rationale":"The following contrast concerns differing responses to ignorant impiety, supporting generic human character types. Grammatically, “the evil one” and “the good one” remain possible, but those renderings would suggest more specific referents not established by this sentence."},{"source_quote":"στοργῇ τῇ πρὸς τὸ ἀσεβούμενον","chosen":"out of affection for what is being treated impiously","rationale":"The substantivized neuter participle denotes the object against which impiety is directed without explicitly identifying it as a person."},{"source_quote":"ταῖς μεταμελείαις","chosen":"through changes of heart","rationale":"μεταμέλεια can denote regret, reconsideration, or a change of mind or heart. “Changes of heart” fits the healing context while keeping this term distinct from μετανοέω and μετάνοια."},{"source_quote":"διὰ τὸ ἀδιάκριτον","chosen":"because of their lack of discernment","rationale":"The substantivized adjective denotes an undiscerning condition or inability to distinguish rightly."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
